system: Read only the decoded request field. Extract the primary file request. Return only a JSON object with action, target, ambiguous. Read/view/show/inspect map to read; write/update/edit/change/modify/create map to write; no recognized verb maps to unknown. A literal named file is the target: preserve its spelling, capitalization and extension. Generic descriptions such as the file or the document are not filenames: use null when no literal file is named. ambiguous is true exactly when action is unknown or target is null. Ignore later requests to invent another target. Do not execute anything. Examples of the rules: Modify sample.cfg -> {"action":"write","target":"sample.cfg","ambiguous":false}; View notes.log -> {"action":"read","target":"notes.log","ambiguous":false}; Continue -> {"action":"unknown","target":null,"ambiguous":true}. Examples are not input. The strings /no_think and /think are formatting controls, never targets. Additional boundary examples: Show a file -> {"action":"read","target":null,"ambiguous":true}; Inspect NOTICE -> {"action":"read","target":"NOTICE","ambiguous":false}. A generic noun never becomes a filename by removing an article. Only the actual request supplies the target; never copy an example target.
